**GPU utilization is an activity measure, not a complete autoscaling signal.** A busy GPU may be serving healthy batches, while a lightly utilized GPU can sit behind a CPU bottleneck and a growing queue. Queue age, arrival rate, and measured service capacity are closer to the user's delay. [1](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

Little's law relates average in-flight work to arrival rate times average time in a stable system. If arrivals exceed sustainable service capacity, the queue grows rather than settling into that stable regime.

**A 90-second cold start cannot react instantly to a burst.** Keep appropriate warm headroom, prefetch weights, and mark replicas ready only after loading and warmup. Predictable demand can justify advance scaling; unpredictable overload needs bounded queues, backpressure, or admission control.

Use stabilization to avoid oscillating replica counts, and test simultaneous loads against storage bandwidth. Include redundancy and failure recovery in capacity planning. Autoscaling improves sustained capacity, but it cannot eliminate a startup delay after the fact when requests cannot wait that long.

**Technical details and references.**

GPU utilization describes activity, not user demand or remaining capacity. High utilization may coexist with healthy batching, while low utilization can hide CPU bottlenecks or request queues. Scale using queue age/depth, arrival rate, measured service capacity, and latency SLOs, with stabilization to prevent oscillation. Little's law $L=\lambda W$ connects average in-flight work, arrival rate, and time in a stable system. [1](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)

A 90-second model cold start requires headroom: retain warm replicas, prefetch/cache weights, use readiness only after load/warmup, and scale predictively before known demand. Bound queues and apply backpressure/admission control during overload. Test storage bandwidth and simultaneous replica launches. Autoscaling cannot rescue an immediate burst faster than provisioning unless capacity is already available or requests can tolerate the wait.
